summary: Verdane, a Norwegian private equity firm, is taking an 11% stake in Meltwater at a €542 million ($592 million) valuation, worth about $65 million, by investing in Fountain Venture, the vehicle controlled by Meltwater founder and chairman Jørn Lyseggen. The structure also gives Verdane an indirect stake in HR firm Jobylon and a partnership for future AI startup investments. The article frames the deal as reflecting pressure on tech valuations, de-risking by investors in a tight European market, and the competitive threat generative AI poses to media monitoring firms.
one_line: Verdane takes an 11% stake in Meltwater, worth about $65M, by investing in founder Jørn Lyseggen's Fountain Venture amid valuation pressure and AI disruption.
key_facts: Verdane is taking an 11% stake in Meltwater at a company valuation of €542 million ($592 million), valuing the stake at around $65 million.
Verdane invests via Fountain Venture, the investment vehicle controlled by Meltwater founder and chairman Jørn Lyseggen, rather than directly in Meltwater.
Verdane closed a $1 billion+ fund earlier in 2023 to invest in scaling tech companies.

Meltwater was publicly traded on the Norwegian stock exchange until earlier in 2023, when it was taken private in a deal with private equity firms Altor and Marlin; Lyseggen kept his remaining share via Fountain.
The take-private deal is the last disclosed valuation and the one Meltwater currently cites.
The Fountain deal also gives Verdane an implied stake in Nordic HR firm Jobylon, whose ARR is around €5 million, versus around €500 million for Meltwater.
Meltwater was founded in Norway but is now headquartered in San Francisco.

Meltwater's market cap of just under $600 million is below the over $700 million it raised as a private startup (per PitchBook) and less than half its valuation at its December 2020 IPO of over $1 billion.
Atomico's report found European funding in 2023 halved to just $43 billion, with private equity firms filling part of the gap left by VC.
Meltwater built AI in-house and acquired businesses in an analytics consolidation play, most notably DataSift, an early Twitter firehose partner whose relationship turned sour.
Generative AI players like OpenAI are seen as a major competitive threat to Meltwater.
Lyseggen called OpenAI's ChatGPT the 'Netscape moment' of a new era and says Meltwater's tech stack is the most modern and AI-centric in its category.
Meltwater says it analyzes around 1 billion documents daily for clients in communications, marketing and PR.
